newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh gas field ablaze after explosion.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh gas field ablaze after explosion.

text.p: Fire engulfed a gas field in northeastern Bangladesh on Sunday where U.S. company Occidental began drilling early this month, fire brigade officials and witnesses said.
Fire broke out at the drilling site following an explosion in a well, they said.
Experts with fire fighting equipment from Singapore would arrive on Monday to try to extinguish the blaze, Energy Secretary Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdhury told Reuters.
He said another expert team from Occidental headquaters in Houston, Texas, would also arrive shortly to assess the extent of damage and find out when drilling could be resumed.
Chowdhury said the government had not received any information about casualties but said there had been extensive damage to equipment.
"The rig was blown off and there was extensive damage," the Energy Secretary said.
Local journalists said several workers at the gas field were injured and vehicles gutted.
Occidental, which has won the right for exploration of hydrocarbon in the Sylhet region, began drilling on June 2.
Energy Ministry officials said the accident occurred when the pipeline of the rig hit a "trap gas" layer at a depth of 840 metres (2,755 feet).
Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan has postponed a scheduled official visit to Iran because of the accident.
Khan and senior officials will visit the accident site on Monday.
Officials in Moulavi Bazar, some 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Sylhet, said they saw fire above the forest at Magurchhara gas field at around 2 a.m.
Railway tracks passing by the gas field also caught fire, disrupting train services.

Journalists said the fire spread over a 2 km (mile) area around the gas field, 20 km (12 miles) from Moulvi Bazar. Police surrounded the whole area and prohibited visits except by experts and officials.
They said some 200 people worked in the Magurchhara gas field. Witnesses told reporters they saw people, many apparently hurt, fleeing the fire.
"The blaze could spread further as surrounding areas are covered with dense forest," one journalist said.
Occidental officials in Dhaka were not immediately available for details.

Occidental was offered the right to search for hydrocarbons in the entire Sylhet region, bordering India's Meghalaya and Assam states, under a Production Sharing Contract (PSC) with the Bangladesh government.
Occidental said it would spend up to $100 million in exploring three out of 23 blocs that Bangladesh has earmarked for foreign hydrocarbon firms.
